predictions.title: Sandboxed-skill verification harness ships as framework default by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the open-source sandboxed-skill verification harness that Anthropic's Claude Code 3.0 Mythos-Preview registry has been running at scale ships as an upstream framework default across the LangChain plus AutoGen plus CrewAI plus Haystack plus Pydantic AI maintainer cohort, exposing the deterministic per-tenant attestation-log audit trail and cross-tenant compositional safety check as a standard framework-side primitive rather than a vendor-private surface. The Wednesday catalysts trace a clean readout that the harness now scales across the full five-paper loader-verification reference set and across seventy gated tenants without timing slip. A Wednesday Anthropic operations note reports Claude Code 3.0 day-thirteen registry telemetry counting roughly 34,400 published skills (up from Tuesday's 32,800, +4.9 percent â€” a seventh consecutive sub-7-percent reading and the first sub-5-percent day of the second week), approximately 2.96M skill installs across the thirteenth 24 hours, and seventy Mythos-Preview gated tenants â€” two business days ahead of the cohort's projected window â€” with two new Continental European public-sector signings on top of Tuesday's Indo-Pacific additions. A Wednesday Simon Willison note documents that the harness's deterministic per-tenant attestation-log audit trail reproduces across all seventy gated tenants with cross-tenant compositional safety checks holding under 55 seconds, and the harness now includes Tuesday's tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step alongside Monday's training-surface checkpoint-provenance step and the standard cross-tenant audit â€” confirming the Verifiable Per-Tenant Capability Attestation paper's demonstration cycle scales cleanly as the loader-verification line composes its full surface. Wednesday's arxiv 2605.07891 consolidation survey gives the harness a single citable end-to-end verification graph spanning training-run checkpoint through agent-loader through tenant-policy gate, and a Wednesday DeepMind note confirms the consolidated Python-and-Rust reference-implementation index now indexes the tenant-policy-attestation manifest alongside the training-surface harness â€” leaving the harness with a fully unified reference-implementation surface to upstream. The framework maintainer cohort's Wednesday Hugging Face Blog post holds the mid-June default-shipment commitment with the tenant-policy-attestation manifest folded in as an optional sixth verification surface, and the Wednesday InfoQ note reports the six-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix conformance test suite holding green across all six vendors for a third consecutive weekday with the same manifest check running on every conformance pass â€” giving framework maintainers a vendor-side conformance signal they can lean on when promoting the harness from optional to default. The structural force is that once the harness reproduces deterministically across seventy gated tenants holding under 55 seconds, the five-paper reference set unifies into one verification graph with one reference-implementation index, and the framework cohort already ships the sixth surface as optional inside mid-June with a six-vendor conformance suite green for three weekdays, the optional-to-default promotion compresses to a release-cycle decision rather than an unsolved engineering question â€” and the mid-June default-shipment ships the full harness as a Q3 2026 followup release. The most likely landing is the open-source harness shipping as a framework default across the maintainer cohort inside Q3 2026, with the Anthropic Mythos-Preview registry continuing to operate the canonical reference deployment, the consolidated DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft reference-implementation index serving as the upstream source-of-truth, and the cross-orchestrator interop matrix's conformance test suite serving as the cross-vendor regression gate. Bear case is that the framework cohort defers the optional-to-default flip to a follow-up minor release inside Q4 2026 if any of the five-paper surface composition checks logs a regression during the mid-June default-shipment dry-run; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the harness as framework default.

reasoning.because: Anthropic harness reproduces across 70 gated tenants under 55s with tenant-policy step layered.
reasoning.given: Framework cohort mid-June ships sixth surface optional; arxiv 2605.07891 unifies the graph.
reasoning.so_that: The open-source verification harness flips from optional vendor-side surface to framework-default upstream primitive.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Haystack, Pydantic AI default it.
reasoning.plain_language: The safety checker that proves an AI tool is genuine will soon be built into the main AI building blocks, not just one vendor's product.

predictions.summary: Wednesday's Anthropic note reports Claude Code 3.0 reaching 70 Mythos-Preview gated tenants with the verification harness reproducing under 55 seconds and the tenant-policy step layered, and arxiv 2605.07891 unifies the five-paper reference set. By Q3 2026 the harness ships as framework default.

predictions.title: AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears 15GW threshold by H2 2026
predictions.body: By H2 2026 the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears a 15GW cumulative threshold, anchored by the third-consecutive-week sovereign-cloud signing cadence and the AI-accelerator IPO comparable set that Wednesday's tape has now firmed into a single readable supply-and-demand picture. The Wednesday catalysts trace a tightening run-up to the T-minus-one-day Thursday May 21 Alphabet analyst day. A Wednesday HPCwire AIwire note reports the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book advancing to near 10.7GW with a fresh weekday sovereign-cloud commitment, the third new commitment of the business week and the highest weekly cadence the book has carried since the program opened. A Wednesday Datacenter Dynamics wire reports the Tenstorrent Galaxy-rack first-half capacity-fulfillment curve crossing the 70-percent threshold for the first time, at roughly 71 percent of the 280-rack target on a cumulative count of 198 racks deployed, with the third European sovereign-cloud increment of the week going to Outscale France plus Atlante Cloud Italy and the third Asia-Pacific increment splitting between Yotta Labs India and CDS Japan. The capital-markets backdrop hardens on the same Wednesday tape: Cerebras CBRS holds the Friday $198.60 close as its reference anchor with the five-desk analyst spread carrying inside a roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging to about 39 percent of float on the analyst-day eve, and a Wednesday 247 Wall St note reporting the Mag-7 preview cohort clearing the 90-percent threshold on Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability â€” the first time the cohort consensus has cleared that line â€” with the cohort treating Wednesday's pre-print Cerebras session as a coincident input. The Wednesday AIwire note further reports Tenstorrent's SEC Corp Fin first-round comment-letter response at its 13-business-day mark inside the staff-review interval with the second-round letter expected late Thursday or Friday, the early-August public-filing target holding, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster steady at six â€” giving equity analysts a fresh three-name AI-accelerator IPO comparable set against which the AMD commitment-book trajectory and the Tenstorrent capacity-fulfillment curve land as the two readable demand-side anchors. The structural force is that once the commitment-book cadence runs at three new sovereign-cloud signings per business week with a sub-10-week run-rate of roughly 0.25GW per signing, the Tenstorrent capacity-fulfillment curve crosses 70 percent five-and-a-half months before the public-filing target with the second-round Corp Fin comment letter inside its staff-review window, and the Mag-7 cohort clears 90-percent breakout-probability against a settled Corp Fin disclosure precedent â€” the capital-and-capacity supply-demand picture compresses to arithmetic that lands the commitment book through 15GW inside H2 2026, well ahead of the program's original end-of-year-2026 marker. The most likely landing is the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clearing 15GW cumulative cleanly inside H2 2026 â€” likely Q3 â€” with the sovereign-cloud cohort accounting for the marginal-signing share above 12GW, the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 going public in early August leaning on the now-71-percent capacity-fulfillment curve as the revenue-traction anchor, and the Mag-7 fiscal-Q3 AI Services breakouts pricing the AMD book as a demand-side comparable. Bear case is that one of the next three sovereign-cloud commitments slips its execution window or the Tenstorrent S-1 ships before the AMD book reaches 12GW, deferring the 15GW landing into early Q4 2026; absent that slip, H2 2026 lands the AMD commitment book through 15GW.

reasoning.because: AMD commitment book advances to 10.7GW Wednesday with a third sovereign-cloud signing this week.
reasoning.given: Tenstorrent capacity fulfillment crosses 70 percent; Mag-7 cohort clears 90-percent breakout line.
reasoning.so_that: The AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears a 15GW cumulative threshold ahead of year-end.
reasoning.landing: By H2 2026; likely Q3; sovereign-cloud cohort drives the marginal-signing share.
reasoning.plain_language: AMD's order book for AI servers is filling so fast it will easily clear 15GW of orders by late 2026.

predictions.summary: Wednesday's AMD note advances the Helios plus MI450 commitment book to near 10.7GW with a third weekday sovereign-cloud signing, Tenstorrent capacity fulfillment crosses 70 percent, and the Mag-7 cohort clears 90-percent breakout probability. By H2 2026 the commitment book clears 15GW.

predictions.title: OECD GENAI reciprocity attestation schema adopts at June 2-6 plenary by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the OECD GENAI cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema clears formal adoption at the June 2-6 working-group plenary or the immediately following written-procedure round, with the now-sixteen-jurisdiction named-candidate cohort plus the originating UK and EU operationalizing the attestation as the common machine-readable layer that frontier-AI vendors emit per tenant â€” turning the perimeter from a manually-tracked named-candidate list into a programmatically queryable interoperability surface. The Wednesday catalysts converge on a clearing-procedure sequence rather than a pivot. A Wednesday andrew.ooo procedural note confirms the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat reporting that member-state schema-comment submissions have passed four-fifths of the named-candidate cohort as the business week's third day cleared, on schedule for the June 2-6 plenary adoption target with the secretariat's schema-comment close keyed to Friday May 29 and the plenary now at T-minus-thirteen calendar days. A Wednesday Decoder reading reports the named-candidate count moving to sixteen on Wednesday with Brunei joining the prior fifteen plus the originating UK and EU as the next adjacent-track Indo-Pacific signal, Qatar's 270-day national-consultation window holding in its second week, no third Gulf Cooperation Council member yet signalling, and the operational recognition threshold remaining the Mythos-class plus GPT-5.5-class capability tier. The vendor implementation surface is already convergent on the same schema: a Wednesday Mistral AI note confirms the cross-orchestrator interop matrix â€” Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry plus Vertex AI Agent Governance Center plus Amazon Bedrock Agent Registry â€” holding its first-week-of-June general-availability target with default support for the now-sixteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field schemas, OpenAI's Wednesday Codex CLI v3.1.7 release folding in optional client-side support for the tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step, and a Wednesday InfoQ note reporting the interop-matrix conformance test suite holding green across all six vendors for a third consecutive weekday with the tenant-policy-attestation manifest check now running on every conformance pass. The structural force is that once member-state comment submissions clear four-fifths of a sixteen-jurisdiction cohort with no third-GCC outlier opening a fresh comment chapter, the secretariat's Friday May 29 comment close lands four business days before the plenary, the cross-orchestrator interop matrix targets its general-availability window for the same first week of June with default tenant-policy schema support, and a four-document academic loader-verification cluster plus its Wednesday consolidation survey have fully settled into a single citable end-to-end surface the Recommendation can reference, the schema's formal adoption compresses to clearing-procedure arithmetic â€” comment-close plus plenary-vote plus written-procedure fallback lands the schema adopted inside Q3 2026 with the originating cohort plus a sixteenth signatory plus an OECD Recommendation text all converging at the same plenary. The most likely landing is the OECD GENAI working-group voting the attestation field schema into a formal OECD Recommendation at the June 2-6 plenary or by written-procedure inside the four-week-following window, with the sixteen-jurisdiction named-candidate cohort plus the UK and EU originating signatories each emitting attestations against the schema before end-Q3 2026, the cross-orchestrator interop matrix shipping general-availability with the schema as a default field, and the United States recognition gap still keyed to the FMRB executive order's signing path running on its own clock. Bear case is one or two member-state submissions deferring into a post-plenary written-procedure round, pushing formal Recommendation adoption into early Q4 2026 with first-cohort attestation emission still landing inside Q3; absent that slip, Q3 2026 lands the OECD GENAI reciprocity attestation schema adopted with the sixteen-jurisdiction perimeter operationalizing it as default.

reasoning.because: OECD GENAI member-state schema-comment submissions clear four-fifths with comment-close Friday May 29.
reasoning.given: Sixteen named candidates plus UK and EU; vendor interop matrix targets early-June GA with default support.
reasoning.so_that: The reciprocity attestation field schema adopts as an OECD Recommendation operationalized across the cohort.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; sixteen jurisdictions plus UK and EU emit attestations against the schema.
reasoning.plain_language: Sixteen countries plus the UK and EU are about to agree on one shared way for AI tools to prove they meet safety rules, ready to use this summer.

predictions.summary: Wednesday's OECD GENAI procedural note clears four-fifths of member-state schema comments with the Friday May 29 close ahead of the June 2-6 plenary, the named-candidate cohort moves to sixteen with Brunei joining, and the cross-orchestrator interop matrix targets early-June GA with default schema support. By Q3 2026 the schema adopts as an OECD Recommendation.
